name: exactextractr
resume: Four exports match installed exactextractr 0.10.1. A grid is an extent and a resolution. A polygon is WKT. GEOS 3.13.1 is called through ctypes. quantile, frac, and weights='area' are not implemented. raster, sf, and terra are not opened. The compiled code is C++, so there is no crate.

functions.name: coverage_fraction
functions.done: Fraction of each cell covered by a polygon. Outside cells are 0 unless crop is true.

check.case: 3 by 3 grid and an axis-aligned square from 0.5 to 2.5

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(raster); library(sf); library(exactextractr) })
one <- function() {
  rast <- raster::raster(xmn=0, xmx=3, ymn=0, ymx=3, nrows=3, ncols=3, crs=NA)
  square <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(c(0.5,0.5, 2.5,0.5, 2.5,2.5, 0.5,2.5, 0.5,0.5), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE))))
  as.matrix(coverage_fraction(rast, square)[[1]])
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
rows <- apply(value, 1, function(row) paste(sprintf("%.17g", row), collapse=" "))
cat(sprintf('{"value":%s,"median_ms":%.17g}\n', paste0("[", paste(sprintf('"%s"', rows), collapse=","), "]"), median(elapsed)*1000))
proof.python:
import json
import statistics
import time
from exactextractr.coverage_fraction import coverage_fraction

def one():
    grid = {"xmin": 0, "xmax": 3, "ymin": 0, "ymax": 3, "nrows": 3, "ncols": 3}
    square = "POLYGON ((0.5 0.5, 2.5 0.5, 2.5 2.5, 0.5 2.5, 0.5 0.5))"
    return coverage_fraction(grid, square)[0]["values"]

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
shown = [" ".join(format(item, ".17g") for item in row) for row in value]
print(json.dumps({"value": shown, "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed)}))

functions.name: exact_extract
functions.done: Summarizes cell values by coverage. quantile, frac, and weights='area' are not implemented.

check.case: mean of cells 1:100 under the man-page triangle

one <- function() {

  poly <- sf::st_as_sfc("POLYGON ((2 2, 7 6, 4 9, 2 2))")

elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf('{"value":%.17g,"median_ms":%.17g}\n', value, median(elapsed)*1000))

functions.name: rasterize_polygons
functions.done: Writes the 1-based index of the polygon with the greatest coverage. A tie keeps the lower index.

check.case: two overlapping squares on a 3 by 3 grid

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(raster); library(sf); library(exactextractr) })
one <- function() {
  g <- sf::st_sf(geometry=sf::st_sfc(
    sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(c(0,0, 2,0, 2,2, 0,2, 0,0), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE))),
    sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(c(1,1, 3,1, 3,3, 1,3, 1,1), ncol=2, byrow=TRUE)))
  ))
  y <- raster::raster(xmn=0, xmx=3, ymn=0, ymx=3, nrows=3, ncols=3)
  as.matrix(rasterize_polygons(g, y))
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
shown <- apply(value, 1, function(row) paste(ifelse(is.na(row), "NA", as.character(row)), collapse=" "))
cat(sprintf('{"value":%s,"median_ms":%.17g}\n', paste0("[", paste(sprintf('"%s"', shown), collapse=","), "]"), median(elapsed)*1000))
proof.python:
import json
import statistics
import time
from exactextractr.rasterize_polygons import rasterize_polygons

def one():
    polys = ["POLYGON ((0 0, 2 0, 2 2, 0 2, 0 0))", "POLYGON ((1 1, 3 1, 3 3, 1 3, 1 1))"]
    grid = {"xmin": 0, "xmax": 3, "ymin": 0, "ymax": 3, "nrows": 3, "ncols": 3}
    return rasterize_polygons(polys, grid)["values"]

value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
shown = [" ".join("NA" if item is None else str(int(item)) for item in row) for row in value]
print(json.dumps({"value": shown, "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed)}))
